gaps.text: Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (The two methods have to sample the same small area and the data have to be brought to a common time step before any joint model; a combined probe head is designed to place both measuring interfaces at one point. Each block keeps its own calibration and diagnostics, and the fused model has to be validated on independent runs and beat the best single method, otherwise the second instrument is not justified.)

Whether the customer's existing laboratory glucose and lactate measurements are a suitable reference for a feasibility comparison, and what their uncertainty and delay are: no supplied page addresses reference-method suitability.
An in situ fiber-probe installation for a cell culture bioreactor (probe type, sterilisation, cleaning): the sources describe in-line fiber probes generally, but no cell culture installation.
Achievable response time, accuracy and detection limit for glucose and lactate in this medium: no supplied page states figures for these analytes.

items.finding: Before fusing data from multiple sources, the contribution of each dataset and its complementarity should be evaluated.
items.how_it_applies: This supports testing whether a second Raman block adds complementary information and whether the fused model beats the best single method before justifying the extended option.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a general PAT data-fusion review; it does not cover cell culture medium, same-area probe alignment, or common time-step requirements.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E02 ¶82

items.finding: Instrument complementarity alone was not sufficient to improve prediction of several CQAs in a Raman and FT-IR food study.
items.how_it_applies: This cautions that adding a second measurement channel may not improve the fused model; independent-run validation against the best single method is needed.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited study is food analytical and uses Raman and FT-IR, not two Raman probes in cell culture; transfer to this medium and probe arrangement is uncertain.

citation.quote: In some situations, instrument complementarity (not data complementarity) was not sufficient to improve the performance of predictive several CQAs, as shown by a Raman and FT-IR data based food analytical study [73].
citation.label: E02 ¶36

items.finding: Contamination of the probe window by a binder during the process can make accurate measurement impossible.
items.how_it_applies: This highlights cleaning and fouling as risks to check when installing an in situ probe in a cell culture bioreactor.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source concerns pharmaceutical unit operations with binder addition, not cell culture medium or sterilisation; the fouling mechanism may differ.

citation.quote: However, an accurate measurement may not be possible because of contamination of the probe window due to the addition of a binder during the process, which is a disadvantage.
citation.label: E03 ¶27

items.finding: Temperature sensitivity of OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests temperature control may need attention for an in situ NIR/MIR installation in aqueous cell culture medium.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a review and refers to tempered sample holders, not in situ fiber probes or cell culture bioreactors; transfer to a sterilised probe installation is uncertain.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E01 ¶12
